Part of the Learning in Harmony Trust
"In the Learning in Harmony Trust, we work in harmony to achieve excellence for all. We live and breathe our values and focus on doing things the right way, providing the perfect environment for all our children to flourish and succeed. And with a diverse range of schools in two contrasting locations, we offer a unique opportunity for professionals looking for a challenging and rewarding career in a supportive, creative and forward-thinking environment." Click here to find out more about the LiH Trust.
Enhancing life through learning
Parent Info
Our Learning
Working @ JFK
Initial Teacher Training
A Warm Welcome
JFK Special School is a founding member of the Learning in Harmony Multi-Academy Trust along with Sheringham Primary School. The school offers specialist provision for pupils with special and additional needs-based across four sites in Newham. Our capacity now is for 139 students in total. Pupils are admitted from Reception to Year 14.The Stratford site offers specialist provision for up to 50 students with sensory and medical needs. This site is equipped with sensory and soft play rooms, as well as large classrooms equipped with tracking hoists and outdoor equipment for students who are more independently mobile. The Beckton site offers specialist teaching and learning for up to 59 students with autism and communication needs. This site has developed its outdoors space and use of local facilities to support independence and life skills and offers a structured teaching and learning approach.The North Woolwich caters for up to 18 younger students with autism and communication needs. The site offers large classrooms, specialist therapy rooms and equipped outside space.
The newly opened Plaistow site offers specialist learning for up to 25 students with autism and communication needs for Secondary - Post 16. The site offers large classrooms, a therapy room and a common room where students can eat lunch and socialise.

Welcome
A welcome to JFK Special School from Jim Robinson, Executive Headteacher.
We are a special school with dedicated sites for profound and multiple learning difficulties (PMLD) and autism spectrum conditions (ASC), full of fantastic, vibrant and incredibly talented students. Our dedicated and highly skilled staff team are passionate about supporting our pupils and each other. Their constant focus on finding new ways to meet our mission statement of enhancing life through learning is a source of inspiration, and something that makes me, personally, very proud.
Covering ages 5-19 we emphasise the importance of communication skills and increasing independence through engaging activities and a class structure that allows us to personalise each student’s learning journey to fit their individual sensory, behaviour, communication, medical and learning needs.
We aim to work in partnership with parents and other professionals as well as enhancing our links in our local community and beyond. As a founding member and the only special school in the Learning in Harmony Trust, we work collaboratively with other schools within the trust to ensure the best possible opportunities and outcomes for all learners.
Whilst this is a brief outline of our school I do hope that the information on the rest of this website provides further detail to answer any questions you might have. If you would like to know more however, please do email our inbox info@jfk.lihtrust.uk or call us on 0208 534 8544 and we will be sure to help. Please also feel free to contact us should you wish to either visit or if you have any suggestions for us to make this site even better.
Jim Robinson, Executive Headteacher

Curriculum
At JFK Special School, we provide a broad, balanced, and personalised curriculum that is carefully adapted to meet the individual needs of every pupil. We support learners across a wide range of ages, abilities, and learning profiles, including students with Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC) and Profound and Multiple Learning Disabilities (PMLD). Our person-centred approach ensures learning is stimulating, enjoyable, and relevant, providing pupils with a rich range of experiences that prepare them for the next stage of their education and adult life.
See below for our Teaching and Learning Framework, which details our four Pathways:
JFK Teaching and Learning Overview
jfk school teaching and learning framework 2026 27.pdf
Every student's learning journey is guided by their EHCP outcomes. Our pathway overviews illustrate how personalised learning goals (PLGs) and curriculum experiences are carefully connected to help each student make meaningful progress towards their individual aspirations.
See below for each pathway overview:
Engagement Curriculum Overview (Click to Open)

Formal Curriculum Overview (Click to Open)

Our curriculum follows a spiral approach, where important skills and knowledge are revisited through a four-year rolling programme of themes, helping pupils build confidence and make meaningful progress. Our themes offer a broad range of experiences while giving pupils regular opportunities to revisit, practise, and apply their skills in different situations. This helps them build confidence, generalise their learning, and make progress over time.

Assessment Overview
Our assessment approach uses ipsative assessment for each pathway. Assessment is supported by a range of tools to help track progress over time, for example, Routes for Learning and the Neuro-inclusive Education Network Progression Framework.
